clue.text: In their own fields the French are unbeatable

definitions.text: In their own fields the French are unbeatable

parts.words: In their own fields the French are unbeatable
parts.note: read as champions, unbeatable in their own fields, and also as the French word for fields, as in the Paris avenue named after the Elysian Fields

explanation.surface: French athletes are said to be unbeatable on home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for fields is the same as the informal short form for champions, so both readings point to one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for champions, who are unbeatable in their speciality; also French for fields.

clue.text: Awkward situation a golfer may get into

definitions.meaning: to be in a fix or a predicament is to be in a tight spot
a golfer aims to sink the ball into the cup on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer finds himself in a tricky spot on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a hole is idiomatic for trouble; a golf hole is what the player plays into.

clue.text: People in serious offence

parts.note: mortals are human beings, people in general
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people are caught up in a grave crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a mortal sin is the gravest kind of wrongdoing, a serious offence.

clue.text: An ABC man, say?

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a 'see' man when spoken: AB plus C (sea) gives a man of the sea

explanation.surface: Someone who has only learned the alphabet, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the crossword abbreviation for an able seaman; the C sounds like sea, so an AB-C man is a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafaring man; AB stands for able seaman and C sounds like sea.

clue.text: Glass apt to shatter in extremis

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer is the noun of 'at the last gasp', at the point of death

indicators.note: breaking glass into pieces suggests the letters of these two words are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A glass liable to break when pushed to the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe the final moment before death or failure, the very end of resources.

clue.text: Unsubstantial, but appropriate as a down clue?

definitions.meaning: having almost no weight or substance
down is fine soft plumage, so a clue about down would suit a phrase about plumage

explanation.surface: A setter wonders whether a flimsy phrase would suit a clue running downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'down' as a grid direction and as soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means weighing next to nothing; down is the lightest plumage of a bird.

clue.text: Joined up, but went on a military campaign without one

indicators.note: here means lacking, so the letter for one is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: soldiered is to have served as a soldier on campaign
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone enlisted, yet marched to war on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined up' seems to mean enlisted, fitting the soldiering surface, but it means fused with metal; 'without' takes I from SOLDIERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldering joins metal parts with a melted alloy, so soldered parts are joined.

clue.text: Get hold of a key file

parts.note: G is a musical key
a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone takes a key and a file, as if planning a jailbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to seize it firmly in the hand, a synonym of grip.

clue.text: Misinform in speech

parts.note: split when spoken into 'Miss in form', a young miss in a school class or form

explanation.surface: To mislead someone by what you say.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class; said aloud, 'Misinform' sounds like 'Miss in form', a girl in a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A young pupil, a miss belonging to a school form or year group.

clue.text: Possibly trifling with one's affections?

indicators.note: signals that the letters of the next word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone may be toying with another's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TRIFLING, and the whole clue describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with someone's affections without serious intent is to court them lightly.

clue.text: See two articles to dislike

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
the indefinite article a
the definite article the

explanation.surface: Reading a pair of newspaper pieces leaves someone cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to dislike it intensely, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Champion golfer's club may be a baptismal gift

parts.note: an apostle is a leading advocate or champion of a cause
a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

explanation.surface: A winning golfer's club is offered as a christening present.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver spoon with a figure of a disciple on its handle, traditionally given at christenings.

clue.text: Ulster may depend on it

parts.note: an ulster is a long heavy overcoat, which hangs from something in the wardrobe

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland's future may rely on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster looks like the Irish province, but here it is a long overcoat, and 'depend' means hang down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe hook-and-bar from which an overcoat such as an ulster hangs.

clue.text: They are engaged in making machines work

definitions.text: They are engaged in making machines work

parts.words: They are engaged in making machines work
parts.note: toothed wheels engage, or mesh, with one another to drive machinery

explanation.surface: Workers employed in getting machinery running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests employed, but it means meshed like gear teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth on gear wheels, which mesh together to transmit motion in a machine.

clue.text: See great changes in overseas accommodation

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before it undergo changes into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices big alterations in housing abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SEE and GREAT. 'overseas accommodation' looks like housing abroad but means cheap berths for a sea crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest passenger quarters on a ship, accommodation for crossing the sea.

clue.text: Foreign city bank headed by a rascal

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bank is topped by the rascal, so that word comes first

parts.note: a rotter is a scoundrel or rascal
a dam is an embankment holding back water

explanation.surface: An overseas bank is run by a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is an earth bank; ROTTERDAM is a Dutch port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch port city is foreign from the point of view of a British setter.

clue.text: Snobs? Rubbish!

definitions.meaning: snob is an old dialect word for a shoemaker or mender of shoes

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea of social climbers with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word is an exclamation meaning nonsense; 'snob' once meant a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe menders were once called snobs, and the word is British slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Half-inclined to stay away — the fly one

definitions.text: Half-inclined to stay away — the fly one

parts.words: Half-inclined to stay away — the fly one
parts.note: a rugby half, the fly-half, has another name meaning inclined to keep aloof

explanation.surface: Someone is half-minded to avoid an annoying insect.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the fly-half is also called the stand-off half; to stand off is to keep one's distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand off means to keep at a distance; the stand-off half is another name for rugby's fly-half.

clue.text: Sailor on northern stretch of water

parts.note: tar is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman sails on a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, the kind of stretch of water found in northern English hills.

clue.text: Wild capers may get you into one

definitions.text: Wild capers may get you into one

indicators.note: describes the next word's letters running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Reckless pranks can land you in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CAPERS, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky predicament or fix, the sort of trouble reckless antics land you in.

clue.text: React badly to girl having a free hand

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: Blanche is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone responds poorly to a girl getting her own way.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a blank paper, the phrase means complete freedom to act as one likes.

clue.text: Artillery unit to show the colours

definitions.meaning: a subdivision of an artillery battery or cavalry squadron
as in ... the colour, parading the regimental flag before ...

explanation.surface: A gun battery parades its flags.
explanation.walkthrough: Trooping the Colour is a British ceremonial parade of a regiment's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit of soldiers; also to parade a flag, as in Trooping the Colour.

clue.text: Work with stitches to heal

definitions.meaning: to make fabric by looping yarn with needles
broken bones join together as they mend

explanation.surface: A wound sewn up so that it will mend.
explanation.definitionFit: To make fabric with needles and yarn, and of a fractured bone, to grow back together.

clue.text: Disregard one note and not another

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
G is a musical note
nor means and not
another note, E

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to one musical note but not to a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no attention, a close synonym of overlook.

clue.text: Setting great store by a spot of publicity

definitions.meaning: stockpiling, laying up a great store of goods
a large board for posting advertisements, a billboard

explanation.surface: Valuing advertising very highly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use the word means a billboard as well as stockpiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockpiling goods, and in British English a large advertising board beside a road.

clue.text: For a difficult problem he asks for a hand

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: Someone stuck on a hard puzzle calls for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asks for a hand' seems to mean seeks help, but it means asks for a hand in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who asks for a woman's hand in marriage is making a proposal.

clue.text: Hostility here, yet I'm resolved about one point

indicators.note: means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the compass letter
something resolved is worked out anew, so the letters of yet I'm are rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Despite ill feeling here, someone has decided on a matter of detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges YETIM into EMITY, and 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is deep-seated mutual ill will, the same as hostility between opponents.
